{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_dc46c315e1934d7880c92129","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge\n2\t\n3\tbead-forge (`bf`) is a repo-local issue tracker built for multi-agent AI coding workflows. Each \"bead\" is a task (bug, feature, research item, etc.) stored as JSON entries in a JSONL file alongside your code. Agents claim beads, work on them, and close them — like a task queue where each worker is an LLM session.\n4\t\n5\t**NOTE:** `bf` is the canonical command. The `br` command name is deprecated — a temporary compatibility alias only. Use `bf` in all documentation, scripts, and examples.\n6\t\n7\tbead-forge is a drop-in replacement for [`beads_rust`](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`) — every `br` command works unchanged. On top of that it adds **atomic claiming** via SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, so 20 workers can claim work simultaneously without racing each other.\n8\t\n9\t```bash\n10\t# Claim the next available bead atomically (no race conditions)\n11\tbf claim --assignee worker-1 --format json\n12\t\n13\t# Split a large bead into children atomically\n14\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 --children '[{\"title\": \"Implement handler\"}, {\"title\": \"Write tests\"}]'\n15\t\n16\t# Show all commands\n17\tbf --help\n18\t```\n19\t\n20\t## The Beads Ecosystem\n21\t\n22\tbead-forge is the third generation of a repo-local issue tracker lineage:\n23\t\n24\t**[beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (Steve Yegge, Python)**\n25\tThe original. A git-backed issue tracker designed as \"memory for coding agents.\" Each issue is a JSON object; every update appends to a JSONL log. SQLite is a read cache, not the source of truth. A DAG of `blocks/blocked_by` dependencies lets `bd ready` return the next actionable task. Designed for single-agent use — no concurrency story at all.\n26\t\n27\t**[beads_rust](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`, Jeffrey Emanuel, Rust)**\n28\tFast Rust port of beads. 10–100× faster than the Python original. Adds `sync --flush-only / --import-only`, a `doctor --repair` command, TOON output format (token-optimized for LLMs), and orphan handling. Maintains full JSONL and `.beads/` compatibility. Our codebase runs a fork of this with a rusqlite shim replacing the upstream FrankenSQLite backend ([upstream issue #171](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/issues/171)). Concurrency story is identical to `beads` — SQLite single-writer, no atomic claiming.\n29\t\n30\t**bead-forge (`bf`, this repo)**\n31\tSuperset of `br`. Preserves 100% of the JSONL format, `.beads/` directory layout, and CLI surface. The `br` command name is a deprecated compatibility alias — `bf` is canonical. Adds atomic claiming, critical-path scoring, velocity tracking, and crash-safe batch operations — the features required for reliable multi-worker fleets.\n32\t\n33\t## Problem\n34\t\n35\t`br` claiming is a client-side read-then-write race:\n36\t\n37\t```\n38\tWorker A: br list → sees bead-123 (open, highest priority)\n39\tWorker B: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n40\tWorker C: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n41\t\n42\tWorker A: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → SUCCESS\n43\tWorker B: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n44\tWorker C: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n45\t```\n46\t\n47\tWith 11+ workers, 10 workers waste cycles on retries. Observed in production: 4 workers simultaneously claiming the same bead, pervasive phantom claims with 20-worker fleets.\n48\t\n49\tThe `br` busy_timeout prevents `database is busy` failures but doesn't prevent the thundering herd. The rusqlite shim fixed SQLite corruption but not contention.\n50\t\n51\t## Solution: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction\n52\t\n53\tbead-forge runs the entire read-score-pick-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:\n54\t\n55\t```sql\n56\tBEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n57\t  SELECT id, priority, critical_path_float\n58\t    FROM issues\n59\t   WHERE status = 'open'\n60\t     AND NOT EXISTS (\n61\t           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n62\t            WHERE d.blocks_id = issues.id\n63\t              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues b WHERE b.id = d.blocked_by_id AND b.status != 'closed')\n64\t         )\n65\t   ORDER BY priority ASC, critical_path_float DESC\n66\t   LIMIT 1;\n67\tUPDATE issues SET status = 'in_progress', assignee = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?;\n68\tCOMMIT;\n69\t```\n70\t\n71\tSQLite's write lock serializes the transaction. The second worker to arrive blocks for ~0.5–2 ms (microseconds of actual work) then picks the next available bead. No phantom claims. No server required — the database file itself is the coordination primitive.\n72\t\n73\t## Architecture\n74\t\n75\t```\n76\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n77\t│                        .beads/                              │\n78\t│  issues.jsonl   ← append-only audit log (source of truth)  │\n79\t│  beads.db       ← SQLite query cache + bf-only tables       │\n80\t│  config.yaml    ← workspace config (bf fields are additive) │\n81\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n82\t          ↑ read/write\n83\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n84\t│                     bf (bead-forge CLI)                      │\n85\t│                                                             │\n86\t│  Claiming  ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic, serialized)     │\n87\t│  Mitosis   ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic split)           │\n88\t│  Batch     ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic multi-op)        │\n89\t│                                                             │\n90\t│  Critical path ── DAG float via recursive CTE               │\n91\t│  Velocity      ── p50/p90 close times per model+type        │\n92\t│  Annotations   ── key/value on any bead                     │\n93\t│  Event log     ── operation history per bead                │\n94\t│  Secret scan   ── pre-commit hook (gitleaks rules)          │\n95\t│  Rotation      ── archive closed beads older than N days    │\n96\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t### bf-only SQLite tables\n100\t\n101\tThese tables are additive — `br` ignores them when operating on a migrated workspace, so `br` and `bf` can be used interchangeably on the same `.beads/` directory.\n102\t\n103\t| Table | Purpose |\n104\t|-------|---------|\n105\t| `bead_annotations` | Arbitrary key/value metadata per bead |\n106\t| `worker_sessions` | Active worker registry (name, model, started_at) |\n107\t| `velocity_stats` | p50/p90 close times per model + harness + issue_type |\n108\t| `critical_path_cache` | Pre-computed DAG float scores (invalidated on dep changes) |\n109\t| `operation_log` | Full event history per bead |\n110\t\n111\t### Data authority: SQLite vs JSONL\n112\t\n113\t**CRITICAL**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n114\t\n115\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n116\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n117\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n118\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n119\t\n120\t**Why the inversion**: Multi-worker fleets need atomic read-modify-write operations (`bf claim`, `bf mitosis`, `bf batch`). These execute inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions on SQLite. JSONL is append-only and cannot support atomic read-write cycles.\n121\t\n122\t**Implication**: Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist **only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n123\t\n124\t### Flush-before-repair rule\n125\t\n126\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. To protect against data loss:\n127\t\n128\t```bash\n129\t# ALWAYS flush first (or use --flush-first)\n130\tbf sync --flush-only\n131\tbf doctor --repair\n132\t\n133\t# OR use the safe flag\n134\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n135\t\n136\t# OR force (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n137\tbf doctor --repair --force\n138\t```\n139\t\n140\tIf unflushed beads exist and neither `--flush-first` nor `--force` is specified, `repair` refuses with an error listing the beads that would be lost.\n141\t\n142\t**Why this matters**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads were permanently lost.\n143\t\n144\t### Claim scoring\n145\t\n146\t`bf claim` selects the highest-priority ready bead using a composite score:\n147\t\n148\t1. **Priority** — P0 always beats P1, etc.\n149\t2. **Critical path float** — among equal-priority beads, pick the one on the longest blocking chain (finishing it unblocks the most downstream work)\n150\t3. **Velocity affinity** — optional: route beads to workers whose historical p50 close time for that `issue_type` is fastest\n151\t\n152\t### Compatibility with br\n153\t\n154\t**The `br` command name is deprecated.** Use `bf` in all new code and documentation.\n155\t\n156\tFor backward compatibility with existing scripts and workspaces, `bf` accepts all `br` commands:\n157\t\n158\t| Command | Behavior |\n159\t|---------|----------|\n160\t| `bf create / list / show / update / close / reopen` | Identical to br, identical JSONL entries |\n161\t| `bf ready` | Same DAG-based filtering; adds critical-path sort |\n162\t| `bf sync --flush-only / --import-only` | Same JSONL format |\n163\t| `bf doctor --repair` | Same repair logic; bf-only tables are not affected |\n164\t| `bf dep / bf label / bf search / bf stats` | Identical |\n165\t\n166\tA symlink `br → bf` allows existing scripts to run unchanged, but new scripts should use `bf` directly.\n167\t\n168\t**Forward-compatibility note**: `bf` adds a `content_hash` column to the `issues` table. bead-forge\n\nbead-forge (`bf`) is a repo-local issue tracker built for multi-agent AI coding workflows. Each \"bead\" is a task (bug, feature, research item, etc.) stored as JSON entries in a JSONL file alongside your code. Agents claim beads, work on them, and close them — like a task queue where each worker is an LLM session.\n\n**NOTE:** `bf` is the canonical command. The `br` command name is deprecated — a temporary compatibility alias only. Use `bf` in all documentation, scripts, and examples.\n\nbead-forge is a drop-in replacement for [`beads_rust`](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`) — every `br` command works unchanged. On top of that it adds **atomic claiming** via SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, so 20 workers can claim work simultaneously without racing each other.\n\n```bash\n# Claim the next available bead atomically (no race conditions)\nbf claim --assignee worker-1 --format json\n\n# Split a large bead into children atomically\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 --children '[{\"title\": \"Implement handler\"}, {\"title\": \"Write tests\"}]'\n\n# Show all commands\nbf --help\n```\n\n## The Beads Ecosystem\n\nbead-forge is the third generation of a repo-local issue tracker lineage:\n\n**[beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (Steve Yegge, Python)**\nThe original. A git-backed issue tracker designed as \"memory for coding agents.\" Each issue is a JSON object; every update appends to a JSONL log. SQLite is a read cache, not the source of truth. A DAG of `blocks/blocked_by` dependencies lets `bd ready` return the next actionable task. Designed for single-agent use — no concurrency story at all.\n\n**[beads_rust](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`, Jeffrey Emanuel, Rust)**\nFast Rust port of beads. 10–100× faster than the Python original. Adds `sync --flush-only / --import-only`, a `doctor --repair` command, TOON output format (token-optimized for LLMs), and orphan handling. Maintains full JSONL and `.beads/` compatibility. Our codebase runs a fork of this with a rusqlite shim replacing the upstream FrankenSQLite backend ([upstream issue #171](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/issues/171)). Concurrency story is identical to `beads` — SQLite single-writer, no atomic claiming.\n\n**bead-forge (`bf`, this repo)**\nSuperset of `br`. Preserves 100% of the JSONL format, `.beads/` directory layout, and CLI surface. The `br` command name is a deprecated compatibility alias — `bf` is canonical. Adds atomic claiming, critical-path scoring, velocity tracking, and crash-safe batch operations — the features required for reliable multi-worker fleets.\n\n## Problem\n\n`br` claiming is a client-side read-then-write race:\n\n```\nWorker A: br list → sees bead-123 (open, highest priority)\nWorker B: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\nWorker C: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n\nWorker A: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → SUCCESS\nWorker B: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\nWorker C: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n```\n\nWith 11+ workers, 10 workers waste cycles on retries. Observed in production: 4 workers simultaneously claiming the same bead, pervasive phantom claims with 20-worker fleets.\n\nThe `br` busy_timeout prevents `database is busy` failures but doesn't prevent the thundering herd. The rusqlite shim fixed SQLite corruption but not contention.\n\n## Solution: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction\n\nbead-forge runs the entire read-score-pick-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:\n\n```sql\nBEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n  SELECT id, priority, critical_path_float\n    FROM issues\n   WHERE status = 'open'\n     AND NOT EXISTS (\n           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n            WHERE d.blocks_id = issues.id\n              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues b WHERE b.id = d.blocked_by_id AND b.status != 'closed')\n         )\n   ORDER BY priority ASC, critical_path_float DESC\n   LIMIT 1;\nUPDATE issues SET status = 'in_progress', assignee = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?;\nCOMMIT;\n```\n\nSQLite's write lock serializes the transaction. The second worker to arrive blocks for ~0.5–2 ms (microseconds of actual work) then picks the next available bead. No phantom claims. No server required — the database file itself is the coordination primitive.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        .beads/                              │\n│  issues.jsonl   ← append-only audit log (source of truth)  │\n│  beads.db       ← SQLite query cache + bf-only tables       │\n│  config.yaml    ← workspace config (bf fields are additive) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n          ↑ read/write\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     bf (bead-forge CLI)                      │\n│                                                             │\n│  Claiming  ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic, serialized)     │\n│  Mitosis   ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic split)           │\n│  Batch     ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic multi-op)        │\n│                                                             │\n│  Critical path ── DAG float via recursive CTE               │\n│  Velocity      ── p50/p90 close times per model+type        │\n│  Annotations   ── key/value on any bead                     │\n│  Event log     ── operation history per bead                │\n│  Secret scan   ── pre-commit hook (gitleaks rules)          │\n│  Rotation      ── archive closed beads older than N days    │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### bf-only SQLite tables\n\nThese tables are additive — `br` ignores them when operating on a migrated workspace, so `br` and `bf` can be used interchangeably on the same `.beads/` directory.\n\n| Table | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `bead_annotations` | Arbitrary key/value metadata per bead |\n| `worker_sessions` | Active worker registry (name, model, started_at) |\n| `velocity_stats` | p50/p90 close times per model + harness + issue_type |\n| `critical_path_cache` | Pre-computed DAG float scores (invalidated on dep changes) |\n| `operation_log` | Full event history per bead |\n\n### Data authority: SQLite vs JSONL\n\n**CRITICAL**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\n**Why the inversion**: Multi-worker fleets need atomic read-modify-write operations (`bf claim`, `bf mitosis`, `bf batch`). These execute inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions on SQLite. JSONL is append-only and cannot support atomic read-write cycles.\n\n**Implication**: Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist **only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n\n### Flush-before-repair rule\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. To protect against data loss:\n\n```bash\n# ALWAYS flush first (or use --flush-first)\nbf sync --flush-only\nbf doctor --repair\n\n# OR use the safe flag\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n\n# OR force (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\nbf doctor --repair --force\n```\n\nIf unflushed beads exist and neither `--flush-first` nor `--force` is specified, `repair` refuses with an error listing the beads that would be lost.\n\n**Why this matters**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads were permanently lost.\n\n### Claim scoring\n\n`bf claim` selects the highest-priority ready bead using a composite score:\n\n1. **Priority** — P0 always beats P1, etc.\n2. **Critical path float** — among equal-priority beads, pick the one on the longest blocking chain (finishing it unblocks the most downstream work)\n3. **Velocity affinity** — optional: route beads to workers whose historical p50 close time for that `issue_type` is fastest\n\n### Compatibility with br\n\n**The `br` command name is deprecated.** Use `bf` in all new code and documentation.\n\nFor backward compatibility with existing scripts and workspaces, `bf` accepts all `br` commands:\n\n| Command | Behavior |\n|---------|----------|\n| `bf create / list / show / update / close / reopen` | Identical to br, identical JSONL entries |\n| `bf ready` | Same DAG-based filtering; adds critical-path sort |\n| `bf sync --flush-only / --import-only` | Same JSONL format |\n| `bf doctor --repair` | Same repair logic; bf-only tables are not affected |\n| `bf dep / bf label / bf search / bf stats` | Identical |\n\nA symlink `br → bf` allows existing scripts to run unchanged, but new scripts should use `bf` directly.\n\n**Forward-compatibility note**: `bf` adds a `content_hash` column to the `issues` table. If the old `br` binary is run directly on a migrated workspace, `br doctor` may emit a column-count mismatch warning. This is cosmetic — data is not affected and `br` reads/writes continue to work correctly.\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\n[NEEDLE](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE) is a fleet orchestrator that spawns LLM-powered workers (Claude Code, GLM variants) to process beads in parallel. bead-forge was built specifically to support NEEDLE fleets at scale.\n\n### How workers claim beads\n\nNEEDLE's `pluck` strand calls `bf claim` instead of the old `br list` + `br update` two-step:\n\n```bash\n# Old (race condition with 11+ workers)\nBEAD=$(br list --format json | jq -r '.[0].id')\nbr update $BEAD --status in_progress --assignee $WORKER\n\n# New (atomic, no race)\nbf claim --assignee $WORKER --format json\n```\n\nA single `bf claim` call acquires the next available bead in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_fc35664500494b90a7180595","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge (`bf`)\n2\t\n3\t![bead-forge hero](hero.png)\n4\t\n5\t**bead-forge** is a Rust CLI for AI-supervised coding workflows. **`bf` is the canonical command.** The `br` command name is deprecated — a temporary compatibility alias only.\n6\t\n7\t---\n8\t\n9\t## The Problem It Solves\n10\t\n11\t`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n12\t\n13\t```\n14\tbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n15\t  ↓  (race window)\n16\tbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n17\t  ↓  (race window)\n18\tbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n22\t\n23\t`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n24\t\n25\t```\n26\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\tThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n30\t\n31\t---\n32\t\n33\t## Architecture\n34\t\n35\t```\n36\tSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n37\t    │                                        │\n38\t    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n39\t    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n40\t    ▼                                        ▼\n41\t  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n42\t  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n43\t```\n44\t\n45\t**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n46\t\n47\t**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n48\t\n49\t---\n50\t\n51\t## Key Features\n52\t\n53\t### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n54\t\n55\t```\n56\tWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\n57\tWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n58\t...\n59\tWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\tThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n63\t\n64\t### Critical Path Scoring\n65\t\n66\t`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n67\t\n68\t```\n69\t$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n70\t\n71\t  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n72\t  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n73\t  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n74\t```\n75\t\n76\t### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n77\t\n78\tWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n79\t\n80\t```bash\n81\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n82\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n83\t         --harness needle \\\n84\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n85\t         --json\n86\t```\n87\t\n88\t`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n89\t\n90\t```\n91\t$ bf velocity\n92\t\n93\tModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\n94\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\n95\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\n96\tclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t### Atomic Batch Operations\n100\t\n101\tReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\n102\t\n103\t```bash\n104\t# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\n105\t# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\n106\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n107\t  --children '[\n108\t    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n109\t    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n110\t  ]' \\\n111\t  --reason \"Split into children\"\n112\t\n113\t# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n114\t# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\n115\tbf batch --json '[\n116\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n117\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n118\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n119\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n120\t  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n121\t]'\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\t**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n125\t\n126\tAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n127\t\n128\t### Extensible Annotations\n129\t\n130\tArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n131\t\n132\t```bash\n133\tbf annotate bf-a3f8 needle_attempt=3 needle_session=abc123 review_status=needs_review\n134\tbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n135\t```\n136\t\n137\t### Operation History\n138\t\n139\t```bash\n140\tbf log bf-a3f8\n141\t\n142\t2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n143\t2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n144\t2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n145\t2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n146\t```\n147\t\n148\t---\n149\t\n150\t### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n151\t\n152\t`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n153\t\n154\t```bash\n155\t# Manual scan\n156\tbf commit-check\n157\t# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n158\t```\n159\t\n160\t**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n161\t\n162\t```bash\n163\t# In your workspace repo\n164\tcat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n165\t#!/bin/sh\n166\tbf commit-check\n167\tEOF\n168\t\n169\tchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n170\t```\n171\t\n172\t**What gets scanned:**\n173\t- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n174\t- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n175\t- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n176\t\n177\t**Patterns detected:**\n178\t- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n179\t- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n180\t- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n181\t- JWT tokens\n182\t- API keys in URLs\n183\t- Database connection strings\n184\t- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n185\t\n186\t**Allowlist exceptions:**\n187\t\n188\tIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n189\t\n190\t```yaml\n191\tsecret_protection:\n192\t  allowlist:\n193\t    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n194\t    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n195\t```\n196\t\n197\t---\n198\t\n199\t## Commands\n200\t\n201\t```\n202\tbf create        --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--label ...]\n203\tbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--format json|text|toon]\n204\tbf show          <id>\n205\tbf update        <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] ...]\n206\tbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\n207\tbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n208\t                 [--workspace <path>] [--any]\n209\tbf critical-path <epic-id>\n210\tbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]']\n211\tbf annotate      <id> key=value [--remove key]\n212\tbf log           [<id>] [--since <date>] [--actor <a>] [--diff]\n213\tbf rotate        [--age-days N]\n214\tbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>]\n215\tbf dep           add-blocker <blocker> <blockee>\n216\tbf dep           tree <id>\n217\tbf label         <id> add <label> [<label> ...]\n218\tbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\n219\tbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--check] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <duration>]]\n220\tbf init          [--prefix <p>]\n221\tbf stats\n222\tbf search        <query>\n223\tbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n224\t```\n225\t\n226\tAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n227\t\n228\t---\n229\t\n230\t## NEEDLE Integration\n231\t\n232\tReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n233\t\n234\t| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n235\t|-----------|--------------|\n236\t| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n237\t| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n238\t| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n239\t| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n240\t\n241\t---\n242\t\n243\t## Compatibility\n244\t\n245\t`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n246\t\n247\t1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n248\t2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n249\t3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n250\t\n251\t---\n252\t\n253\t## Reliability\n254\t\n255\t- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n256\t- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n257\t- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n258\t- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n259\t\n260\t### Data Authority Model\n261\t\n262\t**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n263\t\n264\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n265\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n266\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n267\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n268\t\n269\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite; JSONL is a git checkpoint written only by `bf sync --flush-only`. **Beads created or modified since the last flush exist only in SQLite.**\n270\t\n271\t### Flush-Before-Repair Rule\n272\t\n273\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. Without flushing first, **unflushed beads are silently destroyed**.\n274\t\n275\t```bash\n276\t# Always flush before repair\n277\tbf sync --flush-only\n278\tbf doctor --repair\n279\t\n280\t# Or use the combined command\n281\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n282\t\n283\t# Force repair (with data loss warning)\n284\tbf doctor --repair --force\n285\t```\n286\t\n287\t**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n288\t\n289\t---\n290\t\n291\t## Implementation\n292\t\n293\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n294\t\n295\t- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n296\t- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n297\t- Critical path CTE algorithm\n298\t- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n299\t- Compatibility verification test suites\n300\t- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n301\t\n302\t---\n303\t\n304\t## Migration from br to bf\n305\t\n306\t### Per-Machine Installation\n307\t\n308\t```bash\n309\t# Install bf binary\n310\tcurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n311\t  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n312\t\n313\t# Verify installation\n314\tbf --version\n315\t```\n316\t\n317\t### Per-Workspace Migration\n318\t\n319\t**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\n320\t\n321\t```bash\n322\t# Migrate a single workspace\n323\tbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\n324\t\n325\t# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\n326\tfor workspace in \\\n327\t  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n328\t  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n329\t  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n330\t  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n331\t  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n332\t  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n333\t  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n334\t  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\n335\tdone\n336\t```\n337\t\n338\t**What `bf migrate` does:**\n339\t1. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n\n```\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n```\n\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n\n```\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n```\n\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n    │                                        │\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n    ▼                                        ▼\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n```\n\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n\n---\n\n## Key Features\n\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n```\n\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n\n### Critical Path Scoring\n\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n\n```\n$ bf velocity\n\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n```\n\n### Atomic Batch Operations\n\nReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\n\n```bash\n# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\n# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n  --children '[\n    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n  ]' \\\n  --reason \"Split into children\"\n\n# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n]'\n```\n\n**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n\nAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n\n### Extensible Annotations\n\nArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n\n```bash\nbf annotate bf-a3f8 needle_attempt=3 needle_session=abc123 review_status=needs_review\nbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n```\n\n### Operation History\n\n```bash\nbf log bf-a3f8\n\n2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n\n`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n\n```bash\n# Manual scan\nbf commit-check\n# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n```\n\n**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n\n```bash\n# In your workspace repo\ncat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n#!/bin/sh\nbf commit-check\nEOF\n\nchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n```\n\n**What gets scanned:**\n- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n\n**Patterns detected:**\n- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n- JWT tokens\n- API keys in URLs\n- Database connection strings\n- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n\n**Allowlist exceptions:**\n\nIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nsecret_protection:\n  allowlist:\n    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commands\n\n```\nbf create        --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--label ...]\nbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--format json|text|toon]\nbf show          <id>\nbf update        <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] ...]\nbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n                 [--workspace <path>] [--any]\nbf critical-path <epic-id>\nbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]']\nbf annotate      <id> key=value [--remove key]\nbf log           [<id>] [--since <date>] [--actor <a>] [--diff]\nbf rotate        [--age-days N]\nbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>]\nbf dep           add-blocker <blocker> <blockee>\nbf dep           tree <id>\nbf label         <id> add <label> [<label> ...]\nbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\nbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--check] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <duration>]]\nbf init          [--prefix <p>]\nbf stats\nbf search        <query>\nbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n```\n\nAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n\n---\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\nReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n\n| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n|-----------|--------------|\n| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n\n---\n\n## Compatibility\n\n`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n\n1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n\n---\n\n## Reliability\n\n- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n\n### Data Authority Model\n\n**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite; JSONL is a git checkpoint written only by `bf sync --flush-only`. **Beads created or modified since the last flush exist only in SQLite.**\n\n### Flush-Before-Repair Rule\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. Without flushing first, **unflushed beads are silently destroyed**.\n\n```bash\n# Always flush before repair\nbf sync --flush-only\nbf doctor --repair\n\n# Or use the combined command\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n\n# Force repair (with data loss warning)\nbf doctor --repair --force\n```\n\n**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n\n- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n- Critical path CTE algorithm\n- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n- Compatibility verification test suites\n- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n\n---\n\n## Migration from br to bf\n\n### Per-Machine Installation\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\n```\n\n### Per-Workspace Migration\n\n**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\n\n```bash\n# Migrate a single workspace\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\n\n# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**What `bf migrate` does:**\n1. Acquires migration lock (prevents concurrent claims during migration)\n2. Backs up `beads.db` → `beads.db.br-backup-<timestamp>`\n3. Applies schema migrations (creates bf-only tables via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)\n4. Primes critical_path_cache for all epics\n5. Seeds `config.yaml` with bf-specific defaults if missing\n6. Verifies forward compatibility (br can still open the database)\n7. Verifies backward compatibility (`bf doctor --check` passes)\n8. Releases migration lock\n\n**Dry-run mode** (see what would happen without making changes):\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run\n```\n\n**Recovery mode** (for corrupted/missing databases):\n\nIf `beads.db` is corrupted or missing, `bf migrate --from-jsonl` rebuilds from `issues.jsonl` and reconstructs events from git history:\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --from-jsonl [--seed-velocity]\n```\n\n### Migration Checklist\n\n**Step 1: Per-machine installation**\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\n```\n\n**Step 2: Per-workspace migration loop**\n\n```bash\n# Migrate all workspaces\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Migrating $workspace...\"\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**Step 3: Verify each migration**\n\n```bash\n# Verify each workspace passes doctor check\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Checking $workspace...\"\n  cd \"$workspace\" || continue\n  bf doctor || echo \"  ❌ bf doctor failed\"\ndone\n```\n\nEach `bf doctor` should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n**Step 4: Update NEEDLE adapter configs**\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n### Verification After Migration\n\nFor each workspace, verify both tools can read the database:\n\n```bash\n# Verify bf doctor passes\ncd /path/to/workspace\nbf doctor --check\n```\n\nThis should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n### NEEDLE Integration Update\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n---\n\n## Build & Deploy\n\n### Local Build\n\n```bash\n# Clone and build\ngit clone https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge.git\ncd bead-forge\ncargo build --release\n\n# Install\ncp target/release/bf ~/.local/bin/bf\nchmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify\nbf --help\nbf list\n```\n\n### CI/CD Deployment\n\nBuilt via Argo Workflows on `iad-ci`. This is cosmetic — data is not affected and `br` reads/writes continue to work correctly.","originalFile":"# bead-forge\n\nbead-forge (`bf`) is a repo-local issue tracker built for multi-agent AI coding workflows. Each \"bead\" is a task (bug, feature, research item, etc.) stored as JSON entries in a JSONL file alongside your code. Agents claim beads, work on them, and close them — like a task queue where each worker is an LLM session.\n\n**NOTE:** `bf` is the canonical command. The `br` command name is deprecated — a temporary compatibility alias only. Use `bf` in all documentation, scripts, and examples.\n\nbead-forge is a drop-in replacement for [`beads_rust`](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`) — every `br` command works unchanged. On top of that it adds **atomic claiming** via SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, so 20 workers can claim work simultaneously without racing each other.\n\n```bash\n# Claim the next available bead atomically (no race conditions)\nbf claim --assignee worker-1 --format json\n\n# Split a large bead into children atomically\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 --children '[{\"title\": \"Implement handler\"}, {\"title\": \"Write tests\"}]'\n\n# Show all commands\nbf --help\n```\n\n## The Beads Ecosystem\n\nbead-forge is the third generation of a repo-local issue tracker lineage:\n\n**[beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) (Steve Yegge, Python)**\nThe original. A git-backed issue tracker designed as \"memory for coding agents.\" Each issue is a JSON object; every update appends to a JSONL log. SQLite is a read cache, not the source of truth. A DAG of `blocks/blocked_by` dependencies lets `bd ready` return the next actionable task. Designed for single-agent use — no concurrency story at all.\n\n**[beads_rust](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust) (`br`, Jeffrey Emanuel, Rust)**\nFast Rust port of beads. 10–100× faster than the Python original. Adds `sync --flush-only / --import-only`, a `doctor --repair` command, TOON output format (token-optimized for LLMs), and orphan handling. Maintains full JSONL and `.beads/` compatibility. Our codebase runs a fork of this with a rusqlite shim replacing the upstream FrankenSQLite backend ([upstream issue #171](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/issues/171)). Concurrency story is identical to `beads` — SQLite single-writer, no atomic claiming.\n\n**bead-forge (`bf`, this repo)**\nSuperset of `br`. Preserves 100% of the JSONL format, `.beads/` directory layout, and CLI surface. The `br` command name is a deprecated compatibility alias — `bf` is canonical. Adds atomic claiming, critical-path scoring, velocity tracking, and crash-safe batch operations — the features required for reliable multi-worker fleets.\n\n## Problem\n\n`br` claiming is a client-side read-then-write race:\n\n```\nWorker A: br list → sees bead-123 (open, highest priority)\nWorker B: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\nWorker C: br list → sees bead-123 (same bead)\n\nWorker A: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → SUCCESS\nWorker B: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\nWorker C: br update bead-123 --status in_progress → FAILS (already claimed)\n```\n\nWith 11+ workers, 10 workers waste cycles on retries. Observed in production: 4 workers simultaneously claiming the same bead, pervasive phantom claims with 20-worker fleets.\n\nThe `br` busy_timeout prevents `database is busy` failures but doesn't prevent the thundering herd. The rusqlite shim fixed SQLite corruption but not contention.\n\n## Solution: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction\n\nbead-forge runs the entire read-score-pick-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:\n\n```sql\nBEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n  SELECT id, priority, critical_path_float\n    FROM issues\n   WHERE status = 'open'\n     AND NOT EXISTS (\n           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n            WHERE d.blocks_id = issues.id\n              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues b WHERE b.id = d.blocked_by_id AND b.status != 'closed')\n         )\n   ORDER BY priority ASC, critical_path_float DESC\n   LIMIT 1;\nUPDATE issues SET status = 'in_progress', assignee = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?;\nCOMMIT;\n```\n\nSQLite's write lock serializes the transaction. The second worker to arrive blocks for ~0.5–2 ms (microseconds of actual work) then picks the next available bead. No phantom claims. No server required — the database file itself is the coordination primitive.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        .beads/                              │\n│  issues.jsonl   ← append-only audit log (source of truth)  │\n│  beads.db       ← SQLite query cache + bf-only tables       │\n│  config.yaml    ← workspace config (bf fields are additive) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n          ↑ read/write\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     bf (bead-forge CLI)                      │\n│                                                             │\n│  Claiming  ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic, serialized)     │\n│  Mitosis   ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic split)           │\n│  Batch     ──── BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (atomic multi-op)        │\n│                                                             │\n│  Critical path ── DAG float via recursive CTE               │\n│  Velocity      ── p50/p90 close times per model+type        │\n│  Annotations   ── key/value on any bead                     │\n│  Event log     ── operation history per bead                │\n│  Secret scan   ── pre-commit hook (gitleaks rules)          │\n│  Rotation      ── archive closed beads older than N days    │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### bf-only SQLite tables\n\nThese tables are additive — `br` ignores them when operating on a migrated workspace, so `br` and `bf` can be used interchangeably on the same `.beads/` directory.\n\n| Table | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `bead_annotations` | Arbitrary key/value metadata per bead |\n| `worker_sessions` | Active worker registry (name, model, started_at) |\n| `velocity_stats` | p50/p90 close times per model + harness + issue_type |\n| `critical_path_cache` | Pre-computed DAG float scores (invalidated on dep changes) |\n| `operation_log` | Full event history per bead |\n\n### Data authority: SQLite vs JSONL\n\n**CRITICAL**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\n**Why the inversion**: Multi-worker fleets need atomic read-modify-write operations (`bf claim`, `bf mitosis`, `bf batch`). These execute inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions on SQLite. JSONL is append-only and cannot support atomic read-write cycles.\n\n**Implication**: Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist **only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n\n### Flush-before-repair rule\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. To protect against data loss:\n\n```bash\n# ALWAYS flush first (or use --flush-first)\nbf sync --flush-only\nbf doctor --repair\n\n# OR use the safe flag\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n\n# OR force (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\nbf doctor --repair --force\n```\n\nIf unflushed beads exist and neither `--flush-first` nor `--force` is specified, `repair` refuses with an error listing the beads that would be lost.\n\n**Why this matters**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads were permanently lost.\n\n### Claim scoring\n\n`bf claim` selects the highest-priority ready bead using a composite score:\n\n1. **Priority** — P0 always beats P1, etc.\n2. **Critical path float** — among equal-priority beads, pick the one on the longest blocking chain (finishing it unblocks the most downstream work)\n3. **Velocity affinity** — optional: route beads to workers whose historical p50 close time for that `issue_type` is fastest\n\n### Compatibility with br\n\n**The `br` command name is deprecated.** Use `bf` in all new code and documentation.\n\nFor backward compatibility with existing scripts and workspaces, `bf` accepts all `br` commands:\n\n| Command | Behavior |\n|---------|----------|\n| `bf create / list / show / update / close / reopen` | Identical to br, identical JSONL entries |\n| `bf ready` | Same DAG-based filtering; adds critical-path sort |\n| `bf sync --flush-only / --import-only` | Same JSONL format |\n| `bf doctor --repair` | Same repair logic; bf-only tables are not affected |\n| `bf dep / bf label / bf search / bf stats` | Identical |\n\nA symlink `br → bf` allows existing scripts to run unchanged, but new scripts should use `bf` directly.\n\n**Forward-compatibility note**: `bf` adds a `content_hash` column to the `issues` table. If the old `br` binary is run directly on a migrated workspace, `br doctor` may emit a column-count mismatch warning. This is cosmetic — data is not affected and `br` reads/writes continue to work correctly.\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\n[NEEDLE](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE) is a fleet orchestrator that spawns LLM-powered workers (Claude Code, GLM variants) to process beads in parallel. bead-forge was built specifically to support NEEDLE fleets at scale.\n\n### How workers claim beads\n\nNEEDLE's `pluck` strand calls `bf claim` instead of the old `br list` + `br update` two-step:\n\n```bash\n# Old (race condition with 11+ workers)\nBEAD=$(br list --format json | jq -r '.[0].id')\nbr update $BEAD --status in_progress --assignee $WORKER\n\n# New (atomic, no race)\nbf claim --assignee $WORKER --format json\n```\n\nA single `bf claim` call acquires the next available bead in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. Twenty workers can call `bf claim` simultaneously and each gets a distinct bead in ~1ms.\n\n### Mitosis: crash-safe bead splitting\n\nWhen a worker determines a bead is too large to complete atomically, it splits it into children using `bf mitosis`:\n\n```bash\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n  --children '[\n    {\"title\": \"Implement the handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n    {\"title\": \"Add test coverage\",     \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n  ]' \\\n  --reason \"Scope too large for single session\"\n```\n\nAll operations — create children, wire dependencies, close parent — execute inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. If the process is killed mid-operation, the workspace is left in its original state (parent still open, no orphan children).\n\nNEEDLE's current implementation uses five separate `br` calls with crash-unsafe windows between them. Migrating to `bf mitosis` is a one-function change in `bead_store/mod.rs` — see [`docs/needle-mitosis-migration.md`](docs/needle-mitosis-migration.md).\n\n### Batch operations\n\n`bf batch` lets a worker apply multiple operations atomically:\n\n```bash\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"create\",          \"title\": \"subtask A\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\",        \"child\": \"bf-xyz\"},\n  {\"op\": \"close\",           \"id\": \"bf-xyz\",        \"reason\": \"Decomposed into subtasks\"}\n]'\n```\n\nThe `@0`, `@1` syntax refers to beads created earlier in the same batch — no two-pass coordination needed.\n\n### Velocity tracking\n\n`bf velocity` shows historical close times per model and issue type:\n\n```\nmodel              type    beads   p50      p90\nclaude-sonnet-4-6  task    142     4m 12s   18m 44s\nclaude-opus-4-7    feature  38     22m 05s  1h 12m\nglm-5              bug      91     6m 33s   28m 01s\n```\n\nNEEDLE uses this to route beads: if a `bug`-type bead arrives and a GLM-5 worker is available, it may get priority over a Sonnet worker if GLM-5's p50 for bugs is lower.\n\n## CI/CD and Auto-Deployment\n\nThe `bead-forge-build` workflow template on `iad-ci` builds the binary and publishes releases to GitHub:\n\n1. Builds with `cargo test` and `cargo build --release`\n2. Creates GitHub release with `bf-linux-x86_64` asset\n3. Triggers auto-deployment to lab server\n\n### Auto-deployment mechanism\n\nThe lab server runs a systemd timer (`bf-update.timer`) that checks hourly for new releases and auto-deploys them to `~/.local/bin/bf`:\n\n```bash\n# Check timer status\nsystemctl --user status bf-update.timer\n\n# Manual update\n/home/coding/bead-forge/deploy/bf-update.sh\n```\n\nThe update script:\n- Fetches latest release version from GitHub API\n- Compares to installed version (tracked in `~/.local/bin/.bf-version`)\n- Downloads and installs only if newer\n\nSee `deploy/bf-update.sh`, `deploy/bf-update.service`, and `deploy/bf-update.timer` for implementation.\n\n## Installation\n\nRelease binaries are published to GitHub Releases. On the lab server, a systemd timer auto-deploys new versions hourly. For other machines:\n\n```bash\n# Download latest release\nVERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest | grep -m1 '\"tag_name\"' | sed 's/.*\"tag_name\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/')\ncurl -fsSL \"https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/download/${VERSION}/bf-linux-x86_64\" -o bf\nchmod +x bf\nsudo mv bf /usr/local/bin/bf\n```\n\nOr build from source:\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge\ncd bead-forge\ncargo build --release\ncp target/release/bf ~/.local/bin/bf\n```\n\n## Migrating an existing workspace\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/repo\nbf migrate .beads/\n```\n\nMigration primes the bf-only tables (`bead_annotations`, `worker_sessions`, `velocity_stats`, `critical_path_cache`, `operation_log`) from the existing JSONL data. The workspace continues to work with `br` after migration — bf-only tables are ignored by `br`.\n\n## Commands\n\n**bf is the canonical command.** The br command is a deprecated compatibility alias.\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `bf create / list / show / update / close / reopen` | Core bead operations (br-compatible) |\n| `bf claim` | Atomic claim — picks next ready bead in a single transaction |\n| `bf mitosis <id> --children '[...]'` | Crash-safe split: create children + wire deps + close parent atomically |\n| `bf batch --json '[...]'` | Run multiple operations in one transaction |\n| `bf velocity` | Show p50/p90 close times per model + issue type |\n| `bf annotate <id> --key k --value v` | Attach arbitrary metadata to a bead |\n| `bf log <id>` | Show full event history for a bead |\n| `bf critical-path` | Show longest blocking dependency chain |\n| `bf rotate --older-than 30d` | Archive closed beads older than threshold |\n| `bf migrate .beads/` | Migrate existing br workspace to bf |\n| `bf commit-check` | Pre-commit hook: scan staged .beads/ changes for secrets |\n\n## References\n\n- [beads Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n\n```\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n```\n\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n\n```\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n```\n\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n    │                                        │\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n    ▼                                        ▼\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n```\n\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n\n---\n\n## Key Features\n\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n```\n\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n\n### Critical Path Scoring\n\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n\n```\n$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n\n  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n```\n\n### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n\nWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n\n```bash\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n         --harness needle \\\n         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n         --json\n```\n\n`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n\n```\n$ bf velocity\n\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n```\n\n### Atomic Batch Operations\n\nReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\n\n```bash\n# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\n# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n  --children '[\n    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n  ]' \\\n  --reason \"Split into children\"\n\n# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n]'\n```\n\n**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n\nAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n\n### Extensible Annotations\n\nArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n\n```bash\nbf annotate bf-a3f8 needle_attempt=3 needle_session=abc123 review_status=needs_review\nbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n```\n\n### Operation History\n\n```bash\nbf log bf-a3f8\n\n2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n\n`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n\n```bash\n# Manual scan\nbf commit-check\n# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n```\n\n**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n\n```bash\n# In your workspace repo\ncat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n#!/bin/sh\nbf commit-check\nEOF\n\nchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n```\n\n**What gets scanned:**\n- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n\n**Patterns detected:**\n- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n- JWT tokens\n- API keys in URLs\n- Database connection strings\n- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n\n**Allowlist exceptions:**\n\nIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nsecret_protection:\n  allowlist:\n    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commands\n\n```\nbf create        --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--label ...]\nbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--format json|text|toon]\nbf show          <id>\nbf update        <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] ...]\nbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n                 [--workspace <path>] [--any]\nbf critical-path <epic-id>\nbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]']\nbf annotate      <id> key=value [--remove key]\nbf log           [<id>] [--since <date>] [--actor <a>] [--diff]\nbf rotate        [--age-days N]\nbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>]\nbf dep           add-blocker <blocker> <blockee>\nbf dep           tree <id>\nbf label         <id> add <label> [<label> ...]\nbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\nbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--check] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <duration>]]\nbf init          [--prefix <p>]\nbf stats\nbf search        <query>\nbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n```\n\nAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n\n---\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\nReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n\n| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n|-----------|--------------|\n| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n\n---\n\n## Compatibility\n\n`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n\n1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n\n---\n\n## Reliability\n\n- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n\n### Data Authority Model\n\n**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite; JSONL is a git checkpoint written only by `bf sync --flush-only`. **Beads created or modified since the last flush exist only in SQLite.**\n\n### Flush-Before-Repair Rule\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. Without flushing first, **unflushed beads are silently destroyed**.\n\n```bash\n# Always flush before repair\nbf sync --flush-only\nbf doctor --repair\n\n# Or use the combined command\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first\n\n# Force repair (with data loss warning)\nbf doctor --repair --force\n```\n\n**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n\n- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n- Critical path CTE algorithm\n- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n- Compatibility verification test suites\n- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n\n---\n\n## Migration from br to bf\n\n### Per-Machine Installation\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\n```\n\n### Per-Workspace Migration\n\n**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\n\n```bash\n# Migrate a single workspace\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\n\n# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**What `bf migrate` does:**\n1. Acquires migration lock (prevents concurrent claims during migration)\n2. Backs up `beads.db` → `beads.db.br-backup-<timestamp>`\n3. Applies schema migrations (creates bf-only tables via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)\n4. Primes critical_path_cache for all epics\n5. Seeds `config.yaml` with bf-specific defaults if missing\n6. Verifies forward compatibility (br can still open the database)\n7. Verifies backward compatibility (`bf doctor --check` passes)\n8. Releases migration lock\n\n**Dry-run mode** (see what would happen without making changes):\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run\n```\n\n**Recovery mode** (for corrupted/missing databases):\n\nIf `beads.db` is corrupted or missing, `bf migrate --from-jsonl` rebuilds from `issues.jsonl` and reconstructs events from git history:\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --from-jsonl [--seed-velocity]\n```\n\n### Migration Checklist\n\n**Step 1: Per-machine installation**\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\n```\n\n**Step 2: Per-workspace migration loop**\n\n```bash\n# Migrate all workspaces\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Migrating $workspace...\"\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**Step 3: Verify each migration**\n\n```bash\n# Verify each workspace passes doctor check\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Checking $workspace...\"\n  cd \"$workspace\" || continue\n  bf doctor || echo \"  ❌ bf doctor failed\"\ndone\n```\n\nEach `bf doctor` should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n**Step 4: Update NEEDLE adapter configs**\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n### Verification After Migration\n\nFor each workspace, verify both tools can read the database:\n\n```bash\n# Verify bf doctor passes\ncd /path/to/workspace\nbf doctor --check\n```\n\nThis should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n### NEEDLE Integration Update\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n---\n\n## Build & Deploy\n\n### Local Build\n\n```bash\n# Clone and build\ngit clone https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge.git\ncd bead-forge\ncargo build --release\n\n# Install\ncp target/release/bf ~/.local/bin/bf\nchmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Verify\nbf --help\nbf list\n```\n\n### CI/CD Deployment\n\nBuilt via Argo Workflows on `iad-ci`.
